newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says to curb foreign hotel chains.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says to curb foreign hotel chains.

text.p: Indonesia has said it is to issue a regulation requiring foreign hotel chains to set up local companies in a bid to stop profits flowing out of the country, the Jakarta Post said on Wednesday.

"Hotels managed by international chains have to pay high payments to their headquarters abroad, thereby increasing the country's deficit in its current account," Andi Mappi Sammeng, Director General of Tourism, was quoted as saying.

The regulation, which was first proposed by Indonesia's Tourism, Post and Telecommunications Department around two years ago, will require foreign chains to set up locally managed companies in Indonesia, the newspaper said.
He did not say when the regulation would be issued.
Andi added that the new regulation will also make the management staff of such hotels more accountable to local rules.
"Whenever they are asked to follow local regulations the management of such hotels always excuse themselves, saying they have no right to make decisions," Andi was quoted as saying.
Indonesian tourism department officials said earlier this year that there were 20,453 rooms being managed under 43 international hotel chains, compared to only 10,636 rooms under national chains.
Some hotels have already set up Indonesian firms such as the Hilton International Indonesia, a unit of Hilton Hotels Corp, the Jakarta Post said.
Most international hotel chains operate in Indonesia including the Hyatt Corp, Forte Plc's Meridien, Mandarin Oreintal International and Accor.
